newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euroshares mostly down but Germans hit record.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euroshares mostly down but Germans hit record.

text.p: European bourses slipped on Monday, except in Germany which closed at a record high, as interest rate jitters and a weaker Wall Street encouraged profit-taking after the long bull run.

The dollar retreated from highs early in the day but the nagging worry for both equity and foreign exchange markets was whether an interest rate rise will emerge from a U.S. Federal Reserve committee meeting starting on Tuesday.
Economists expect no rate rises when monetary authorities meet on both sides of the Atlantic this week, including the two-day meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FMOC).

But few investors are confident enough to take chances, in London and Paris at least, as the FMOC meeting will open on the third anniversary of an unexpected U.S. rate hike which sent share prices tumbling around the globe.
British and French investors found plenty of excuses to stay on the sidelines on Monday or take profits after their markets closed at record highs on Friday.
By late afternoon on Monday, London's FTSE-100 index was down 18 points at 4,257.8 while in Paris, the CAC-40 was off 8.01 at 2,508.01.
An unpredictable Wall Street, which started sliding late on Friday and opened weaker again on Monday, provided the immediate depressant.
By the European close, the Dow Jones industrial average was down 18.86 points at 6,794.23. Wall Street dealers blamed relatively weak data from U.S. purchasing managers.

London particularly was also dampened by domestic factors. Stuart Weatherby, economist at Panmure Gordon, said British investors were beginning to focus on the approaching company results season and the effect of a strong pound on exporters.

But interest rate anxiety still nagged investors. "I still get the impression that interest rates will not be going up either in the UK or the U.S." Weatherby said. "Although I think they should do, in both."
German shares were the notable exception. The blue chip DAX-30 index ended the floor session up 27.14 points, or 0.9 percent, at a record high of 3,062.29.

But dealers said the gains were in relatively thin volumes, mainly led by dollar-sensitive firms like Daimler-Benz AG as the U.S. currency traded firmly above 1.64 marks. The broader market was cautious.

The dollar slipped from its intraday highs after the data from U.S. purchasing managers showed a bigger than expected drop in the January index, although it remained above levels late on Friday in Europe.
The dollar was at 1.6435 marks and 121.70 yen at late afternoon, weaker than in the morning but up from 1.6365 and 121.12 in late European trade on Friday.
Dealers were also keeping an eye on a meeting of deputy finance ministers from the Group of Seven (G7) industrial nations in Frankfurt.
The deputy ministers are preparing the agenda for a meeting of G7 finance ministers and central bank governors at the weekend.

A report from the European statistics agency Eurostat, which assessed accounting practices European Union governments have used to meet the criteria for monetary union (EMU), had little effect on the mark.
It said that central bank gold sales could not be used for cutting deficits to meet criteria laid down in the Maastricht treaty.
Gold bounced up about $1.00 after the Eurostat report from earlier prices. Dealers said the news confused the market but did not erase fears of future central bank sales.
By late afternoon bullion was at $346.25 an ounce compared with Friday's late European level of $344.60.
CURRENCIES AT 1630 GMT
The dollar was at 1.6435 marks and 121.70 yen, up from 1.6365 marks and 121.12 yen in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed 18.0 points down at 4,257.8.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 27.14 points at a record high of 3,062.29.
PARIS - The CAC-40 finished down 8.01 points at 2,508.55.
PRECIOUS METALS - Gold closed at $346.30 an ounce after being fixed at $343.75 and against $344.60 at Friday's close.Silver was unchaged at $4.92.
